capitals.name: Rangpur
capitals.note: 'Rangpur (1707-1794)'; held by the Moamoria rebels in 1769-1770 and 1788-1794.

Infobox area 41,957.8 km2 for 1826; the drawn shape, clipped to Assam, is about 51,000 km2 (ratio 1.2) and ignores the Matak tract's autonomy from 1805 and the Burmese occupation 1822-1826 (hatched in the ledger).

region.text: Upper Assam round Charaideo, the land Sukaphaa settled

ledger.note: 1228: Sukaphaa arrives at Khamjang and founds the Ahom kingdom in Upper Assam. 'Foundation traditionally dated to the arrival of Sukaphaa: Traditionally 1228'; 'conventionally dated from 1228 to 1826', a date the page itself disputes. Sukaphaa's centre Charaideo is dated 'traditionally 1253'.

1397: Sudangphaa moves the capital to Charagua. 'Charaideo (traditionally 1253-1397)', 'Charagua (1397-?)'; 'Sudangphaa established a new capital at Charagua'. The page names Bakata on the Dihing as Suhungmung's capital without a year.
1512: Suhungmung annexes Habung. 'He annexed Habung, a Chutia dependency in 1512.'
1513: the Chutia war begins. The Chutia king Dhirnarayan 'attacked the Ahoms at Dikhoumukh the next year, but was unsuccessful'; the Ahom page: a clash with the Chutia kingdom 'began in 1513'.

1523: the Chutia kingdom falls. Suhungmung annexed 'the rest of the Chutia Kingdom' in '1523-24' after building a fort at Dibrugarh in 1522; the Ahom page: 'culminated in its annexation in 1523' (an officers' list says 1524).

region.text: the Chutia kingdom: Sadiya, Lakhimpur and the upper Brahmaputra

ledger.note: 1523: the Chutia kingdom is annexed. 'annexed the rest of the Chutia Kingdom' in '1523-24'; the Ahom page has 1523 (and 1524 in an officers' list).

1526: Marangi is taken from the Kachari kingdom. A Marangi list gives 'acquired from the Kachari kingdom in 1526'; 'In 1531 Khunkhara, the Kachari king, sent forces under his brother Detcha to drive the Ahoms away from Marangi' (Suhungmung page).

region.text: the Kachari border country up to the Kolong

ledger.note: 1536: the Kachari frontier is settled at the Kolong. 'In 1536, after the series of contacts with the Kachari kingdom,' Ahom rule extended 'up to the Kolong River'.

region.text: the country up to the Kolong river

ledger.note: 1536: Ahom rule reaches the Kolong. 'In 1536, after the series of contacts with the Kachari kingdom,' Ahom rule extended 'up to the Kolong River'.
1540: the capital is Garhgaon. Infobox 'Garhgaon (1540-1707)'.

region.text: the north bank east of the Barnadi up to Singiri

ledger.note: 1615: the Mughals fall on the Ahom frontier. 'In November 1615, Abu Bakr suddenly fell upon Kajali, the Ahom frontier post on the southwest'; the Mughals 'came to regard the territory east of Barnadi up to Singiri as part of the conquered region'.

region.text: the north bank east of the Barnadi

ledger.note: 1639: the treaty of peace. 'a treaty of peace was signed in February 1639' between Momai Tamuli Borbarua and Allah Yar Khan; the Ahoms accepted that 'western Assam commencing from Gauhati passed into the hands of the Mughals'.

region.text: the territories east of the Barnadi in the north

ledger.note: 1639: the Mughals renounce the country east of the Barnadi. They 'gave up all pretensions to the territories east of Barnadi in the north and Kalang in the south'; the page does not say who held the north bank before.

region.text: Guwahati and Kamrup to the Manas

ledger.note: 1658: the Ahoms retake Guwahati. 'expelled the Mughals from Gauhati, and chased them down beyond the river Manaha'. [Reviewer sa-04-x, 2026-10-19: year corrected from 1648: the Ahom-Mughal page puts the expulsion under Jayadhwaj Singha (1648-1663) 'taking advantage of the emperor Shah Jahan's illness and the war of succession', and 1648 there is only his accession; the Jayadhwaj Singha page: 'After the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan fell sick in 1658' the Ahoms 'pushed west and took control of the region up to the Sankosh river'. Confidence 2: the event page gives no year]

1662: Mir Jumla takes Guwahati. 'Mir Jumla entered Assam in the beginning of 1662'; 'Pandu, Guwahati, and Kajali fell into the hands of the Mughals practically unopposed.' The cession was formalised at Ghilajharighat in January 1663.

1662: the Mughals hold Garhgaon. 'Abandoning his capital and his all treasures, the ahom king Jayadwaj fled'; 'Only Garhgaon and Mathurapur remained in the possession of Mughals' in the later campaign.

1663: the treaty of Ghilajharighat. 'a treaty was concluded at Ghilajharighat in January 1663'; 'the Ahoms ceded western Assam to the Mughals' and 'Jayadhwaj Singha transferred Kamrup to the possession of the Mughals'; the page does not date the Mughal withdrawal from Garhgaon.

region.text: Itakhuli and Guwahati, Kamrup to the Manas

ledger.note: 1667: the Ahoms recapture Guwahati. 'On 2 November 1667, Itakhuli and the contiguous garrison of Guwahati fell into the hands of the Ahoms.' Aurangzeb heard of it in December and sent Ramsingh; the Ahoms kept it at Saraighat in 1671.
1679: Laluk Barphukan hands Guwahati to the Mughals. 'in March Laluk Sola made over Gauhati to the Mughals' for four lakhs of rupees.

region.text: Guwahati and Kamrup to the Manas

ledger.note: 1682: the Mughals are ousted at Itakhuli. 'After nearly seventy years of sustained efforts, the Mughals were finally ousted in the Battle of Itakhuli in 1682'; 'the Ahom forces chased the defeated Mughals nearly one hundred kilometers back to the Manas river', which 'then became the Ahom-Mughal boundary until the British occupation'.
1707: the capital is Rangpur. Infobox 'Rangpur (1707-1794)'.

1769: the Moamoria rebels take Rangpur. 'On November 21, 1769, the rebels occupied the Ahom capital and placed Ramakanta, son of Naharkhora, on the throne.' Raghav Moran had been flogged on 15 September 1769.
1770: the royalists retake Rangpur. Ragha was killed on 14 April 1770 'some of the old nobility in disguise killed Ragha'.

1788: the rebels besiege Rangpur and the king flees to Guwahati. The rebels 'surrounded Rangpur in January 1788'; in August 1788 Patkonwar retook it 'but his victory was short-lived', and Captain Welsh 'captured Rangpur in March 1794', so the rebels are read as holding it from 1788.
1794: the capital is Jorhat. Infobox 'Jorhat (1794-1826)'.

1794: Captain Welsh captures Rangpur. 'Captain Welsh captured Rangpur in March 1794'; the British were recalled and Purnananda Burhagohain became de facto ruler. The infobox moves the capital to Jorhat in 1794.

region.text: the Bengmara (Matak) tract of the Moran country

ledger.note: 1805: the Matak tract becomes a tributary. Sarbananda 'accepted a peace deal' and was 'given autonomous command of the Bengmara region'; his family paid annual tribute to the Ahom kingdom; 'The Moamaria rebellion thus ended with the creation of a near-independent Matak tract ruled by a Barsenapati.'

region.text: the whole kingdom, a Burmese province under a military governor

ledger.note: 1822: the Burmese take Assam. Chandrakanta 'surrendered to Tilwa at Assam Chokey' in June 1822; 'the Burmese declared Mingimaha Tilwa the Raja of Assam and brought an end to the sovereign Ahom rule'; a garrison of 2,000 stayed.
1826: the Matak tract passes to the British with the rest. The page gives no end for the tribute relation; 1826 is the end of the kingdom (bridging).

1826: the Burmese leave Assam. 'after the Treaty of Yandabo in 1826, the control of the kingdom passed into British hands'; 'This treaty marked the end of Burmese rule and the beginning of British rule in Assam.'

1826: Yandabo ends the Ahom kingdom. 'conventionally dated from 1228 to 1826'; 'Britain seizes control: 1826'. Purandar Singha is listed as ruler 1833-1838 in the infobox (a restoration the page does not explain).

wars.name: Ahom-Chutia war
wars.outcome: Suhungmung annexed the Chutia kingdom in 1523-24.

wars.name: Ahom-Kachari conflict

zones.text: Marangi and the country to the Kolong

wars.outcome: The Ahoms held Marangi from 1526 and reached the Kolong in 1536; the Kachari king Khunkhara attacked Marangi in 1531.

wars.name: Turbak's invasions
wars.outcome: The first Muslim invasion of 1527 was pushed back to the Burai river; Turbak of Gaur advanced in April 1532, was killed near the Bharali and his army pursued 'till the Karatoya'; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Koch-Ahom conflicts
wars.outcome: Listed in the infobox as 'Koch-Ahom conflicts: 1543-68'; the pages opened give neither a zone nor an outcome.

wars.name: Ahom-Mughal wars

zones.text: Kamrup between the Barnadi and the Manas
the north bank east of the Barnadi

wars.outcome: Barnadi and Kalang fixed by the 1639 treaty; Guwahati changed hands in 1658, 1662, 1667, 1679 and 1682; the Manas became the boundary after Itakhuli.
wars.note: Mir Jumla's invasion (1662-63) ended in the treaty of Ghilajharighat (January 1663), Ramsingh's campaign (1667-1671) at Saraighat (1671).

wars.name: Moamoria rebellion
wars.outcome: Rebels held Rangpur in 1769-1770 and from 1788 to 1794; the rebellion ended in 1805 with a near-independent Matak tract.

wars.name: Burmese invasions of Assam
wars.outcome: Three Burmese invasions (1817, 1819, 1821-1822); the Burmese took Assam in June 1822 and left under the Treaty of Yandabo in 1826.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on any page for the early kingdom; the Naga and Patkai frontiers are approximate.
The Mughal frontier is fixed by name: the Barnadi and Kalang (treaty of 1639) and the Manas (after Itakhuli, 1682); the hill frontiers stay soft.
The Moamoria, Matak and Burmese episodes leave the extent uncertain.

notes:
No Cliopatria row (Cliopatria lacks the Ahom kingdom). Five pages: Ahom kingdom, Suhungmung, Ahom-Mughal conflicts, Moamoria rebellion, Burmese invasions of Assam. The Ahom-Mughal page was read twice (the second for 1648, 1667 and 1639). Rulers are omitted: the Ahom page lists only some swargadeos (Sukaphaa 1228-1268, Sudangphaa 1397-1407, Suhungmung 1497-1539, Pratap Singha 1603-1641, Suramphaa 1641-1644, Gadadhar Singha 1682-1696, Rudra Singha 1696-1714, Siva Singha 1714-1744, Pramatta Singha 1744-1751, Rajeswar Singha 1751-1759 or 1769, Lakshmi Singha 1769-1780, Purandar Singha 1833-1838).
Area: the infobox gives 41,957.8 km2 for 1826; the 1682-1826 shape (circles round Dibrugarh, Jorhat, Nagaon, Tezpur and Dispur clipped to Assam) comes to about 51,000 km2 (ratio 1.2 to the infobox, within the factor of two); a gap-filler could tighten it to the Brahmaputra valley.
Disagreements: Chutia annexation 1523 (Ahom page) against 1523-24 (Suhungmung page) and 1524 (an officers' list); Marangi from the Kachari in 1526 (a Marangi list) against 1536 (text) and the Kachari attack of 1531; Rajeswar Singha's reign 1751-1759 against 1751-1769; the Ahom page's founding date 1228 is 'traditional' and disputed.
Not settled: the Koch-Ahom conflicts of 1543-1568 (no zone or result); the early boundary (the page gives none); the Naga overlordship of 1504 and the Aitonia Nagas (no region); Kamrup between 1639 and 1648 (who held it); the year Mughals left Garhgaon in 1662-63; Burmese hold in 1817-1819; the date of Yandabo (24 February 1826 is not on the pages opened); the Matak tract's end.
Counterparts needing a dossier: chutia-kingdom (to 1523), kachari-kingdom (Dimasa), koch-dynasty (Kamata/Koch Bihar), moamoria-rebels (type rebel: Rangpur 1769-1770 and 1788-1794), matak-kingdom (Bengmara, 1805-1826), mughal-empire and konbaung-dynasty (Cliopatria's Konbaung ends 1819, before the 1822 occupation).
Gazetteer names needed: Nagaon. [Reviewer sa-04-x, 2026-10-19: the Guwahati recovery moved from 1648 to 1658 (ledger, keyframes 5-6, war outcome); see the ledger note]
